meta.source: UK Annual Statement of Trade, imports 1872-1899
meta.measure_note: Origins are the country/port whence goods were CONSIGNED (shipped) to the UK, NOT the place of production. Entrepots (Holland, Belgium, Gibraltar, Hong Kong) therefore overstate as "origins".
meta.quantity_note: National totals are the Tier-1 anchor. Origin cells are de-duplicated: where a parent line and its breakdown (e.g. United States + its Atlantic/Pacific coasts) both appear, only the finer level is counted, so origins no longer double-count against the anchor. Per-origin values remain provisional.

flag_note.noorig: no origin the gazetteer can place — the map stays blank
flag_note.transposed: the printed page was a list of commodities, not of origins, so the origin column has been suppressed — only the national total is shown
flag_note.noval: no value figures — only the quantity measure works
flag_note.nounit: the printed unit was not captured, so quantities may mix units and the axis is unlabelled
flag_note.oneyear: origins for a single year only
flag_note.noanchor: no national total published for this line, so the origins cannot be checked against one
flag_note.gapyears: some years inside the series have a national total but no origin table at all - the map goes blank for them while the trade was real
flag_note.nooverlap: the national total and the origin tables cover different years, so neither has ever been checked against the other
flag_note.overanchor: origins add up to more than the national total — residual double-counting
flag_note.underanchor: origins add up to less than half the national total — the map shows part of the trade
flag_note.resid: most of the trade is consigned from origins the gazetteer cannot place

France.note: principal consignment via Le Havre (also Bordeaux/Marseille)

Germany.note: German Empire; consignment via Hamburg (also Bremen)

Holland.note: Netherlands; Rotterdam/Amsterdam entrepot — much is re-consignment, not Dutch production

Spain.note: placed at Bilbao (iron ore); Spanish trade also ships from Seville/Valencia/Malaga

Portugal, Azores, And Madeira.note: Portugal incl. its Atlantic islands (Azores, Madeira)

Russia.note: Russian Empire; placed at St Petersburg (Baltic)

Sweden And Norway.note: union of Sweden and Norway (1814-1905); pre-split combined line

Austrian Territories.note: Austria-Hungary (Habsburg Empire); Adriatic consignment via Trieste/Fiume

Turkey Proper.note: Ottoman core, distinct from Ottoman dependencies

Gibraltar.note: British entrepot at the strait — mostly transit trade

United States Of America.note: placed at New York (dominant Atlantic shipment port)

United States Of America (Atlantic).note: US goods shipped from Atlantic ports — New York etc.

United States Of America (Pacific).note: US goods shipped from Pacific ports — San Francisco

Canada.note: British North America / Dominion of Canada; placed at Montreal (St Lawrence grain/timber)

Brazil.note: Rio de Janeiro (also Santos for coffee)

United States Of Colombia.note: historical federal name for Colombia (to 1886); placed at Cartagena

Central America.note: isthmus states as a printed group

British West India Islands.note: British Caribbean colonies as one line

British East Indies.note: colonial umbrella for British India (Bombay/Madras/Bengal presidencies) and sometimes the Straits & Ceylon; placed inland as an aggregate

China.note: placed at Shanghai; scope varies by era (pre-1885 "China and Hong Kong")

Hong Kong.note: British free port; largely transit trade for South China

Aden.note: British coaling station / Red Sea entrepot

Asiatic.note: unspecified Asiatic origins as a printed group

British Possessions In South Africa.note: Cape Colony + Natal (wool); pre-1891 combined line, later split

Western Africa (Foreign.note: non-British West African coast (OCR-truncated); placed at Accra

West Africa Portuguese Possessions Not P.note: Portuguese West Africa (Angola); Luanda; OCR-garbled label

Australasia.note: umbrella for the Australian colonies + New Zealand

Canary Islands.note: Spanish Atlantic islands; Las Palmas (bananas, tomatoes)

The Gold Coast.note: British West Africa; Accra (palm oil, later cocoa)

Niger Protectorate.note: Niger delta / Oil Rivers, British West Africa (palm oil)

Bolivia.note: consignment via the Pacific coast (silver, tin)

British West Africa.note: the British West African settlements as one printed line (Gambia, Sierra Leone, Gold Coast, Lagos); placed at Lagos

Portuguese Possessions In Western Africa.note: Portuguese West Africa (Angola, Cabinda, Portuguese Guinea); Luanda

East Coast Of Africa.note: the East African coast as one printed line (Zanzibar, the Swahili coast, Mozambique); placed at Zanzibar

Islands In The Pacific.note: Pacific islands as one printed line (Fiji, the Friendly and Navigator Islands); placed at Levuka/Suva, Fiji

Tripoli And Tunis.note: the Ottoman/French North African coast printed as one line; placed between Tunis and Tripoli
